movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's net profit excluding Notable Items — its cash-comparable core measure — fell 2% to $6,972m in FY25 from $7,113m in FY24, a $141m decline (ev-1, ev-53). The bank's own summary: revenue $22.5bn, up 3% from $21.8bn (ev-56); net operating income $22,464m vs $21,763m, +3% (ev-4); pre-provision (operating) profit $10.5bn, down 3% from $10.8bn (ev-57, ev-6). Statutory net profit was $6,916m, down 1% from $6,990m (ev-11, ev-52, ev-17); the only item separating statutory from ex-Notable profit was hedging items (a $56m reduction in FY25 vs $123m in FY24) — no asset sales, remediation, restructuring or write-down Notable Items in either year (ev-54, ev-55). Westpac frames it as "higher operating income and lower credit impairment charges more than offset by higher expenses" (ev-12). Its FY24–FY25 walk: NII +$557m, non-interest income +$144m, expenses -$972m, impairment +$113m, tax & NCI +$17m (ev-46). The cost-to-income ratio ex Notable Items rose to 53.0% from 50.3% (ev-35, ev-6).

drivers.columns: FY24 vs FY25 walk bar; FY Sept 2025 less FY Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: NII rose 3% to $19,473m from $18,916m, "driven by growth in average interest earning assets" (ev-2, ev-13). AIEA up 3% to $1,002.9bn, with business loans +11% and housing +2%, partly offset by lower personal loans and the runoff and sale of the auto finance portfolio (ev-20, ev-23). Core NII +3% to $18,191m; Treasury & Markets down 2% to $1,282m (ev-19, ev-22).

drivers.bank_label: Core NIM down 1bp, Treasury & Markets NIM flat
drivers.narrative: Not separately quantified in dollars by the bank. Group NIM ex Notable Items fell 1bp to 1.94% from 1.95%, core NIM 1bp to 1.81% from 1.82%, Treasury & Markets NIM impact flat at 0.13% (ev-21). Westpac says "Balance sheet growth was partly offset by lower net interest margin" and Treasury & Markets fell on "a stronger performance from Treasury in the prior year" (ev-22, ev-47).

drivers.columns: FY24 vs FY25 walk bar; FY Sept 2025 less FY Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Non-interest income up 5% to $2,991m from $2,847m "due to higher fee, Markets and wealth management income" (ev-3, ev-14). Net fee income +4% to $1,732m on card fees and higher business and Institutional lending fees from a larger balance sheet (ev-24, ev-27); net wealth management +8% to $476m on higher funds under administration (ev-25, ev-28); trading and other +7% to $783m on rates and FX (ev-26, ev-29).

drivers.columns: FY24 vs FY25 walk bar; FY Sept 2025 less FY Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: HEADLINE expenses rose 9% to $11,916m from $10,944m (ev-5, ev-35). UNDERLYING (ex the $273m restructuring charge) the rise was $699m, or 6%, to $11.6bn (ev-58, ev-35). Westpac's expense walk: staff costs +$397m, technology +$146m, volume and other +$199m, investments +$359m (UNITE investment $399m, amortisation up $106m), productivity -$402m (simpler operating model, reduced property footprint, digitisation) (ev-60, ev-67, ev-68, ev-64). Staff expenses +7% to $6,326m on wage growth, UNITE and investment in bankers; technology +13% to $3,136m; occupancy -7% to $652m; other -3% to $1,529m (ev-30, ev-32, ev-36, ev-37, ev-38, ev-39).

drivers.bank_label: Fit for Growth restructuring expenses (inside expenses; NOT a Notable Item)
drivers.narrative: Pre-tax restructuring charge of $273m in 2H25 (nil in FY24) "to support targeted productivity initiatives under our Fit for Growth program" (ev-34, ev-15). It sits inside the -$972m expense bar, not outside it, so it is a sub-part, not an additive driver. Westpac's Notable Items table shows Restructuring costs of nil in both years — the only Notable Item is hedging (ev-55, ev-54), so this charge is fully inside the ex-Notable result.

drivers.columns: FY24 vs FY25 walk bar; FY Sept 2025 less FY Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Charge fell 21% to $424m from $537m, 5bps of average loans down from 7bps (ev-7, ev-40, ev-43). "The lower impairment charge was mainly due to an increase in write-backs and recoveries partly offset by a higher CAP charge" (ev-43): IAPs, write-backs and recoveries swung to a $34m benefit from a $140m charge, while total CAPs rose to $458m from $397m (ev-41, ev-42). Recoveries $247m mostly in credit cards and personal loans (ev-45); the results book adds "an increase for new portfolio overlays" as a partial offset (ev-16).

drivers.columns: FY24 vs FY25 walk bar; FY Sept 2025 less FY Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: A small $17m benefit. Income tax expense fell 1% to $3,135m from $3,169m (ev-8), partly offset by $17m of profit attributable to non-controlling interests in FY25 (nil in FY24) (ev-9). The effective tax rate rose to 31.0% from 30.8%, "mainly due to benefits from prior period tax adjustments in Full Year 2024 not repeated in Full Year 2025", and remains above the 30% Australian corporate rate (ev-44, ev-18).

notable_items: Hedging items: -$56m post tax in FY25 vs -$123m in FY24 — the ONLY Notable Item in either year; a statutory-to-ex-Notable reconciliation item, not a bridge driver (ev-54, ev-10)
Fit for Growth restructuring expenses $273m pre-tax in 2H25 (nil FY24) — expensed inside the ex-Notable result, explicitly NOT classified as a Notable Item (ev-34, ev-55)

disagreements.explanation: Westpac has printed no cash measure since 1H23; net profit excluding Notable Items is its core management measure. The two movements differ because hedging items (unrealised fair value on non-qualifying economic hedges and hedge ineffectiveness) were a $56m reduction in FY25 against $123m in FY24, a $67m favourable swing that flatters statutory relative to ex-Notable profit. Ex-Notable is the headline row for this task; statutory is quoted beside it.

limitations: The bank publishes no cash earnings measure; net profit excluding Notable Items is treated as cash-comparable and is a non-AAS, unaudited, unreviewed measure by Westpac's own statement (ev-1 page text).

The adopted walk (IDP p40) bars are after-tax-equivalent only in aggregate: NII, non-interest income, expenses and impairment bars are pre-tax movements and the tax effect sits in the single 'Tax & NCI' bar, so the components are not individually tax-adjusted contributions to net profit.
Volume and margin within NII are not quantified in dollars by the bank; only the +557 total bar, AIEA growth (3%) and NIM (-1bp) are disclosed, so nii.volume and nii.margin cannot be split in $m.

The expenses bar is a net number: Westpac reports $402m of productivity savings offsetting gross increases (staff +$397m, investments +$359m, volume and other +$199m, technology +$146m), and says productivity 'provided a partial offset'. The -$972m headline therefore understates gross cost pressure.

The $273m restructuring charge is disclosed as a sub-part of the expenses bar, not as a separate walk bar, so it must not be added to the -$972m; showing it as a separate quantified component risks double counting and it is flagged as such.

The impairment bar of +113 is a net movement: a swing to a $34m IAP benefit from a $140m charge was partly offset by a higher CAP charge ($458m vs $397m) including an increase for new portfolio overlays and a 5 percentage point rise in the downside scenario weight.

The results announcement does not publish its own FY24-FY25 profit bridge chart; the adopted walk is the slide/IDP chart (p40), corroborated component-by-component by results-book tables on pages 9, 11, 16, 18 and 21.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased by 3% driven by growth in average interest earning assets.
Non-interest income was up 5% due to higher fee, Markets and wealth management income.

Operating expenses were 9% higher. The increase included restructuring costs of $273 million to support targeted productivity initiatives under our Fit for Growth program. Excluding these costs, operating expenses increased 6% mainly due to higher staff costs and the step up in UNITE investment spend. Productivity provided a partial offset.

Credit impairment charges of $424 million represented 5 basis points of average gross loans compared to 7 basis points of average gross loans in the prior year. The decrease reflected a reduction in new IAPs and higher write-backs and recoveries, which was partly offset by an increase for new portfolio overlays.
Statutory net profit was $6,916 million, a decrease of 1%. Notable Items, related to hedging items, were a reduction of $56 million compared to a reduction of $123 million in the prior period.
The effective tax rate of 31.0% was slightly higher than the Australian corporate tax rate of 30%, due to certain non tax deductible expenses.

Net interest income increased 3% to $19,473 million. Key drivers included: • Higher core net interest income, up 3% to $18,191 million. Balance sheet growth was partly offset by lower net interest margin; • Treasury and Markets income, down 2% to $1,282 million due to a stronger performance from Treasury in the prior year.

Average interest-earning assets increased by 3% to $1,002.9 billion, including growth of 11% in business loans and 2% in housing loans. This was partially offset by the reduction in personal loans and the runoff and subsequent sale of the auto finance portfolio in March 2025.
Net fee income increased by 4% to $1,732 million reflecting an increase in card fees and higher business and Institutional lending fees from a larger balance sheet.
Net wealth management income increased by 8% to $476 million from higher funds under administration.
Trading and other income increased by 7% to $783 million reflecting higher sales and risk management income, including rates and foreign exchange.

Total operating expenses increased 9% to $11,916 million. The increase included a restructuring charge of $273 million in the Second Half of 2025 to support targeted productivity initiatives under our Fit for Growth program. Excluding this charge, operating expenses increased by 6% due to the ramp up in UNITE investment, wage growth and higher software amortisation. Lower occupancy costs provided a partial offset. The expense to income ratio excluding Notable Items was 53.0%, up from 50.3%.
